andro-rasanter-r42: Soft, forgiving backhand rubber; mushy, lacking forehand power.
andro-rasanter-r47: Spinny backhand rubber some prefer to G-1; blocking suffers.
butterfly-dignics-05: Fast, spinny and very durable; too fast to control on blocks.
butterfly-dignics-09c: Tacky, very spinny and great short; hard and fast on the backhand.
butterfly-fan-zhendong-alc: Fast carbon with real feedback and control; stiff for some.
butterfly-glayzer-09c: A softer, more forgiving Dignics 09C; mushy, and the grip fades.
butterfly-harimoto-innerforce-alc: Forgiving carbon with a big sweet spot; slower than Viscaria.
butterfly-harimoto-innerforce-super-alc: Faster than the ALC yet precise; beginners may struggle.
butterfly-innerforce-layer-alc: Controllable and fast for pushing and looping; muted at first.
butterfly-petr-korbel: Fast 5-ply wood with great feel; heavy, with a thin handle.
butterfly-primorac: All-wood control for years; too slow as players improve.
butterfly-timo-boll-alc: Fast carbon with power on loops; unforgiving near the table.
butterfly-viscaria: Crisp, fast and great on backhand; hard to control for beginners.
dhs-fang-bo-b2x: Inner carbon speed with touch at strong value; hollow for a few.
dhs-hurricane-3: Slow and very spinny; demanding, and the tack fades.
dhs-hurricane-3-neo: Spinny, linear looper's favourite; needs full-body strokes.
dhs-hurricane-3-neo-national: Tacky with strong spin when boosted; demanding, grip fades.
dhs-hurricane-301: Near all-wood feel with extra power; the slim handle lets it down.
dhs-hurricane-8-80: Tacky backhand rubber that needs no boosting; sheets run heavy.
dhs-power-g7: Great-value all-wood first blade; narrow handle, a bit heavy.
donic-baracuda: Grippy, high-throw backhand rubber; dated or slow for a few.
nittaku-acoustic: All-wood feel and feedback that lasts years; thin handle.
nittaku-acoustic-carbon-inner: More power and sweet spot than the Acoustic; stiffer for one.
nittaku-fastarc-c-1: Softer, forgiving G-1 for backhand; bouncy or mushy for a few.
nittaku-fastarc-g-1: Controllable, durable and spinny; the bouncy arc is tricky.
stiga-allround-classic: Soft, lively blade for learning spin; slow, and some outgrow it.
stiga-cybershape-carbon-cwt: Fast with a big sweet spot and weights; hard and direct.
stiga-cybershape-wood: Good feel and a balance of speed and control.
stiga-infinity-vps-v: Fast, controlled wood for a first custom setup; too fast for a few.
tibhar-evolution-mx-s: Spinny on both sides and lasts; the hard sponge needs big swings.
tibhar-hybrid-k3: Tacky, springy and cheaper than Dignics 09C; it wears out fast.
tibhar-quantum-x-pro: Safe, spin-insensitive and controlled; softer and slower.
tibhar-stratus-power-wood: All-wood control kept for years; the large head is heavy.
victas-curl-p1v: Pips rated highly for chopping and defence; hard to control.
victas-triple-double-extra: Very spinny and fast; the tack fades within weeks.
yasaka-ma-lin-carbon: Control, grip and speed for fans; stiff as a plank to others.
yasaka-ma-lin-extra-offensive: All-wood attacking penhold favourite; short, thin handle.
yasaka-rakza-7: Controllable, spinny and durable for beginners; bouncy at max.
yasaka-rakza-xx: Grippy and spinny for strong players; demanding for several.
yasaka-rakza-z: Tacky hybrid with spin and short game; many call it heavy.
yasaka-sweden-classic: All-wood feel and control, not fast, so good for beginners.
yasaka-sweden-extra: Slow, soft and very controllable; several dislike the thin handle.
